pure-announcement.rationale: A tool README, not launch or funding coverage, and its core observation — AI assistants leave machine-detectable linguistic markers of incompleteness (deferrals, hedging, stubs) orthogonal to what syntax linters catch — transfers beyond the antislop binary.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (evals, Cypher querying, OSV, wide events, CycloneDX, LLM wiki) touch linting AI-generated code for intent gaps.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The mechanism is an open-source pattern/AST linter whose behavior and benchmarks are reproducible from the repo, even if 'zero false positives' is marketing.

durability.rationale: The detection surface is a list of current AI writing tics ('for now', 'should work') that erodes as generation habits change, and much of the note is millisecond benchmark tables, install matrices, and per-language support levels that will drift.

actionability.rationale: It equips a reader to act without the product — treat deferral/hedging comments as a CI-blocking signal on AI-written code, and keep that check disjoint from what eslint/clippy already catch — down to the pattern taxonomy and severity gating.

atomicity.rationale: One idea throughout: lint for the intent-gap markers AI code leaves behind; it states in a single paragraph without the README's tables.
